content:
Rob Lowe is opening up about his much-scrutinized decision to take on a starring role in “Confession,” a new movie written by conservative commentator Ben Shapiro.

Appearing on the “Second Thought” podcast Tuesday, the Emmy- and Golden Globe-nominated actor said he had no qualms about working with Shapiro, founder of the right-wing media company The Daily Wire and an outspoken supporter of President Donald Trump.

“I called Ben and said, ‘This is fantastic,’” Lowe explained.

When Shapiro asked if his conservative reputation would deter Lowe from joining the movie’s cast, the actor was quick to shrug off the suggestion: “I said, ‘I’ve worked with the most left-wing writers in the world. Why wouldn’t I also work with the most right-wing writers in the world?’”

“Confession,” released last week on The Daily Wire’s streaming service, takes place in Russia circa 1938, under the dictatorship of Joseph Stalin. Lowe stars as Alexi, a literature professor who is arrested and interrogated by a KGB agent, Vladimir (James Franco), who happens to be one of his former students.

In a separate interview on the “Conversations With Coleman” podcast that aired Monday, Shapiro acknowledged that Lowe actively pursued the role of Alexi, but admitted he had some of his own reservations about the former “West Wing” star’s casting.

“You’re Rob Lowe. If you ask to play a part, the answer is yes, but I’m just telling you, you’re way too handsome for this,” Shapiro recalled.

Describing “Confession” as “challenging” and “a tough watch,” Lowe said many of his representatives weren’t jazzed by the project, despite the fact that the cast also includes Emile Hirsch, Jennifer Jason Leigh and Nick Nolte.

“There were people who were definitely like, ‘Are you crazy?’ But… I’m old enough, established enough, people know me well enough, to know that I’m not an ideologue at all,” he said. “I’ve campaigned for Republicans. I’ve campaigned for Democrats… Jane Fonda was at my 25th birthday party, for fuck’s sake. So I have my bona fides in both worlds.”

He also hoped “Confession” would be picked up by a major production company like Focus Features or optioned by Netflix after getting some buzz on the film festival circuit. To his surprise, he said the response from potential distributors was “absolute crickets.”

“A lot of people cannot see a work just for its work,” he lamented. “They have to do the math of: ‘What does it mean? What will people think? Does that mean I’m on this side or does that mean I’m on that side?’”

Whether Lowe and his co-stars’ gamble on working with Shapiro will pay off remains to be seen. Early reviews of “Confession” have been less than glowing, with The Hollywood Reporter calling it: “Torture, onscreen and off.”
